answer: Each identity holds vote power that decays unless restored by payment. It locks a 60-credit bond, starts full, and loses 10% per epoch without a key-bound top-up. At dawn, a velvet ledger lists decayed identities for audit. The k-th top-up by one operator in an epoch costs 12+2(k-1) credits and needs a distinct task proof that is unreusable, so 1,000 fakes cost 1,011,000 credits, not 12,000. A rented-replenishment ring fails because a proof signed for one vertex cannot restore another, and reuse burns that bond. An honest agent pays 60 and 12 per epoch for one identity.
